title: Rapid validate-and-scale playbook for customer POC
content:
Purpose:
This is a field-friendly, lightweight playbook for running a fast customer POC (2–4 weeks) with an emphasis on rapid validation and safe scale. Intended audience: SE, Solutions, Customer Success, Eng-SRE backup.

High-level outcome (customer-facing):
- Demonstrate an end-to-end Redwood inference flow for target workload with measurable latency and cost per 1k tokens, plus a plan to achieve production SLAs.

Top success criteria (must be agreed by customer in kickoff):
1) Functional: end-to-end demo that exercises the main API calls and expected traffic pattern (sample traffic generator + 1 integration).
2) Performance: median tail latency <= 500ms for 512 token samples under steady-state 8 rps or equivalent for customer's baseline.
3) Cost/throughput: estimate of tokens/sec and projected monthly token cost within 20% of target.
4) Quality guardrails: no >5% reproducible regressions vs customer test prompts (evaluation harness).
5) Handoff: SE -> Customer Success runbook and a minimal infra runbook checked in repo.

Quick assumptions and constraints (state these in kickoff):
- Customer will provide a sanitized sample dataset (10–20k examples) by Day 2.
- Access to a test environment or temporary VPC peering must be setup by infra on Day 3.
- We will use a Redwood-hosted model variant unless customer insists on private.

Week-by-week plan (2-week rapid track; 4-week extended track notes inline):
- Day 0 (pre-kickoff): send pre-read with sample prompts, consent, and security checklist.
- Day 1 (kickoff, 90m): align goals, confirm success criteria, agree data sharing, and schedule hands-on workshop.
- Day 2: SE runs sample ingestion test; customer delivers dataset.
- Day 3: infra/network setup + temporary credentials.
- Day 4-5 (workshop sprint): 3-hour hands-on session:
  - 0-30m: architecture walkthrough (runtime, routing, quantization options)
  - 30-90m: ingest sample dataset and run baseline evals
  - 90-150m: tune batching/cache settings and run perf tests
  - final 30m: capture metrics, open issues, next actions
- Day 6-8: iterate on failing evals, triage flaky prompts, produce performance report draft.
- Day 9-10: deliver interim report + replayable script for customer to run.
- Day 11-14 (if 2-week): finalize findings, create handoff playbook, schedule executive demo.

If extended to 4 weeks, Weeks 3–4 add: stress tests (burst scenarios), canary rollout plan for Dedicated, and security/compliance checklist completion.

Task tracker (owner shorthand):
- Kickoff prep pack: Aisha (owner)
- Network/VPC setup: Marco (infra lead)
- Data ingestion script and sanitizer: Jonah
- Baseline eval harness + metrics dashboard: Evelyn
- Performance tuning (batch/kv/cache): SE paired (Aisha + Jonah)
- Cost estimate and quantization recommendation: Marco + Evelyn
- Final runbook and CS handoff checklist: Priya

Acceptance checklist for each task (use checkbox in artifact repo):
- [ ] Repro script exists and runs in <=30m on clean machine
- [ ] Evaluation harness produces deterministic pass/fail for baseline set
- [ ] Dashboard shows 95th/99th percentiles and cost breakdownper-token
- [ ] Security: customer-approved list of outbound endpoints and creds rotation plan

Operational readiness rubric (quick heatmap):
- Observability: basic metrics + traces (OK / Needs work / Missing)
- Failover: fallback to cheaper model variant defined (OK / Needs work / Missing)
- Autoscaling: baseline policy defined (OK / Needs work / Missing)
- Incident runbook: on-call + escalation path (OK / Needs work / Missing)

Risk register (short):
- Data delivery delayed (mitigation: run with synthetic dataset, re-run on customer dataset later).
- Network/VPC windows blocked by customer security (mitigation: request temporary IP allowlist and share stubbed flow).
- Quality regression beyond tolerance (mitigation: quick rollback to earlier model, propose prompt engineering changes).
- Unclear success criteria (mitigation: require sign-off in kickoff minute).

Decision log (append-only, capture owner initials and date):
- 2026-01-22 AP: Use Redwood-hosted model variant for initial validation (customer OK with hosted).
- 2026-01-24 MR: Agree to 2-week rapid track unless dataset >50k rows.

Workshop agenda (detailed for Day 4):
- 10:00 Intro + goals (10m)
- 10:10 Architecture and runtime primer (20m)
- 10:30 Data and eval setup (30m)
- 11:00 Baseline runs and interpret metrics (30m)
- 11:30 Tuning knobs deep dive (45m)
- 12:15 Break (15m)
- 12:30 Perf runs and heatmap (45m)
- 13:15 Risk & rollout discussion (30m)
- 13:45 Next steps & owners (15m)

Artifacts we will deliver (minimum):
- run-commands.sh (replayable script)
- eval-baseline.csv and eval-summary.md
- perf-heatmap.png + cost-projection.xlsx
- SE handoff-playbook.md (runnable checklist)

Handoff checklist for CS (Priya to confirm):
- [ ] Demo script and recording uploaded
- [ ] Known issues and triage tips documented
- [ ] Post-POC pricing model recommended
- [ ] Follow-on engagement template (SLA/commit options) attached

Notes to self / open questions (capture during kickoff):
- Customer may require on-prem model variant for GDPR datasets — decision deadline Day 3.
- Which internal SLA level will customer purchase if POC passes? (affects routing policies and capacity planning)
- Are there any internal security reviewers who must join the workshop?

Next immediate actions (first 48h):
1) Send kickoff pre-read + consent form (Aisha, by EOD).
2) Confirm network contact and expected firewall windows (Marco).
3) Create skeleton eval harness repo and invite collaborators (Jonah).

Notes on collaboration pattern: keep tickets small and time-boxed; call out blockers in daily 15m sync. Use #se-poc-{customer} Slack channel and tag eng-sre on infra blockers.

Appendix: minimal command snippets (example to run locally)
- ./run-commands.sh --dataset sample.json --model rwd-4b --batch 16 --output results.json
- python3 eval/harness.py --gold gold.csv --pred results.json --metrics precision,recall,f1

End of doc — append incremental logs here during the engagement.
